steps.say: Sales Charts opens from the Charts button on the Sales Analysis tab. Here it shows the R M of Hanover's sales, uploaded from a C S V, with a vacant lot on Birchwood Lane in Mitchell as the subject. It is live: every filter change in the main window updates these charts. The status line reports how many sales arrived and how many are ticked.

Company signs every chart with your firm name in the caption. Size unit switches between acres, square feet and front feet, and the unit is remembered. If a tab looks empty, the first thing to check is the unit.
Rates can be nominal or time-adjusted to the effective date. Trend basis uses the fitted trend from the sales themselves, or a rate per year you type.
Distance from chooses the subject parcel or Portage and Main as the reference for the distance plots. Trim to percentiles drops the extremes from the fits without excluding the sales.
Freeze stops live updates while you read or capture. Table view shows the numbers behind the charts. Show excluded brings unticked sales back as hollow points.

The filter waterfall explains the count. Sales loaded, then after the Sales Analysis filters, then unticked in the grid, then the agricultural consistency filters, so you can always say why a sale is not on the chart.
Four pages: Land Price per Unit, Agricultural, Total and Per Lot Price, and Water. Each has a row of maps and a row of charts. Every card has a P N G button that renders it at report size.
